title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Following the Cash — 10-Year Financials, Working Capital & Earnings Quality
question: Do GNA Axles' 10-year financial statements prove genuine cash compounding, or do working-capital absorption and modest ROCE cap its intrinsic quality?

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion, cash flow is a fact, and return on capital employed is the final judge of both.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Let us review the multi-year audited ledger from Screener consolidated statements [1]. From FY15 to FY26, GNA grew revenue from ₹430 Cr to ₹1,478 Cr. TTM sales through September 2026 hit ₹1,778 Cr [1]. Net Profit grew more than five-fold from ₹22 Cr to ₹117 Cr, reaching ₹145 Cr TTM [1]. Two P&L facts stand out. First, OPM% never fell below 13% in any year of the decade. Second, depreciation nearly tripled from ₹23 Cr (FY15) to ₹70 Cr (FY26) as GNA reinvested in presses and CNCs, while interest stayed low at ₹7–14 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY15–TTM, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Consistent 13%–16% OPM across a full decade of freight and tractor cycles, with H1 FY27 driving TTM sales to a record ₹1,778 Cr and TTM PAT to ₹145 Cr [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Fortification & Zero-Dilution Equity Growth

web_blocks.html: GNA's balance sheet is its quietest strength—though H1 FY27 footnotes reveal rising working-capital liabilities and dormant-subsidiary monitoring items. Total Reserves grew nearly ten-fold from ₹98 Cr (FY15) to ₹1,031 Cr (September 2026), lifting total equity to ₹1,074 Cr [1]. Equity Capital rose from ₹21 Cr in FY23 to ₹43 Cr in FY24 via a 1:1 bonus share issue, doubling share count to 4.29 Cr shares with zero dilutive equity raises [1][25]. Borrowings stood at ₹203 Cr in September 2026 (down from ₹259 Cr in March 2025), lowering Debt/OPBDIT to 0.7x and supporting ICRA's November 13, 2026 reaffirmation of [ICRA]AA- (Stable) [1][33]. However, Other Liabilities jumped 52% in six months from ₹298 Cr (March 2026) to ₹453 Cr (September 2026; up from ₹206 Cr in March 2025), nudging TOL/TNW from 0.5x to 0.6x, while CWIP climbed to ₹55.2 Cr [1][33][35]. Consolidated statements also include two pre-revenue, auditor-unreviewed subsidiaries—GNA Axles Inc. (Michigan) and GNA Mobility Limited (immaterial ₹5.31 lakh H1 loss; ₹25 Cr board-approved investment / ₹80 Cr planned outlay)—whose future capex deployment requires footnote tracking [4][35][38].

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY15–Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Net worth has compounded to ₹1,074 Cr with zero dilutive equity raises since the 2016 IPO and borrowings fell to ₹203 Cr by Sep 2026, though Other Liabilities jumped to ₹453 Cr alongside rising receivables and CWIP [1][33][35].

web_blocks.html: Now let us test earnings quality by comparing Operating Cash Flow (CFO) against EBITDA and Capex. Across FY16–FY26, GNA posted positive CFO in ten out of eleven years. Only FY17 was negative at -₹90 Cr during post-IPO working-capital expansion [1]. From FY18 through FY26, GNA generated ₹834 Cr of cumulative CFO against ₹784 Cr of Net Profit (matching the sum of annual P&L rows), a healthy ~106% CFO-to-PAT conversion. Free Cash Flow tells a tighter story: GNA spent ₹28–155 Cr a year on fixed assets, so cumulative FCF over FY18–FY26 was modest (₹54 Cr total across the FCF row, with FY26 alone supplying +₹56 Cr after -₹2 Cr cumulative across FY18–FY25) [1]. Crucially, FY26 CFO and FCF (₹214 Cr / +₹56 Cr) benefited from Days Payable stretching +53 days (76d to 129d) rather than structural receivable collection [1]. The October 23, 2026 H1 FY27 cash flow statement confirms this reversion: H1 FY27 CFO compressed to ₹61.15 Cr against ₹82.34 Cr of H1 PAT (74.3% conversion) as rapid sales expansion absorbed working capital—proving growth in heavy forging remains capital-hungry [4][35]. Worse, if stretched supplier credit (129 Days Payable in FY26 and ₹453 Cr Other Liabilities in September 2026) unwinds toward FY22–FY25 norms (76–89 days) during a revenue pause, working-capital outflows could flip annual CFO negative just as in FY17 (-₹90 Cr) [1][35].

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY15–FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cumulative CFO tracks reported PAT (~106% over FY18–FY26), but FY26 FCF (+₹56 Cr) benefited from +53d payable stretching (76d→129d), and H1 FY27 CFO reverted to ₹61.15 Cr vs ₹82.34 Cr PAT (74.3% conversion) [1][4][35].

web_blocks.title: Working Capital Ratios & The ROCE Ceiling

web_blocks.html: The Ratios table below explains why GNA earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict rather than a compounder badge. Over the past decade, ROCE stayed in a 14% to 21% corridor. It sat at 14.3% in FY26, with ROE at 12.2% [1]. Why can't a company with 16% OPM and low debt break above 22%–25% ROCE? Look at working capital: Debtor Days rose from 116–130 days (FY16–FY19) to 151 days in FY25 and FY26 [1]. That pushed Cash Conversion Cycle to 139 days and Working Capital Days to 133 days (ICRA NWC/OI near 40%) [1][33]. Further, the October 23, 2026 H1 FY27 balance sheet shows Trade Receivables rose 19.9% in six months—from ₹582.55 Cr in March 2026 to ₹698.27 Cr in September 2026 (~143 days on TTM sales of ₹1,778 Cr) [1][4][35]. Over the same period, inventories surged 42.7% YoY to ₹312.64 Cr [4][35]. Ownership filings also clarify the 9.96 pp promoter stake drop. Maninder Singh Seehra exited fully on September 29, 2026, and Harjinder Kaur trimmed her shares after a 2024 family settlement separating GNA Axles under Ranbir Singh Seehra from unlisted GNA Gears [1][12][37]. Still, promoters carry a 5.49% share pledge (13.80 lakh shares) as of September 30, 2026 [12][37]. On ₹1,778 Cr of TTM sales, cutting debtor days by 20 days would free nearly ₹97 Cr in cash—almost half of GNA's ₹203 Cr debt [1]. Until collections tighten without payable stretching, capital intensity keeps returns in the mid-teens.

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Working Capital & Capital Efficiency Ratios (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: 151 FY26 Debtor Days, ₹698.3 Cr H1 FY27 Trade Receivables, and ~40% NWC/OI cap GNA's ROCE at 14%–21% (14.3% in FY26; ROE 12.2%), reinforcing disciplined cyclical underwriting [1][4][33][35].

book_paragraphs: Every forensic review ends with one question: does the accounting profit turn into spendable cash, and at what return on capital? Let us open GNA Axles' ten-year books from FY15 through the October 23, 2026 H1 FY27 balance sheet and follow the cash rupee by rupee [1][4][35].

On the surface, the P&L and leverage profile are remarkably resilient. Revenue expanded from ₹430 Cr in FY15 to ₹1,478 Cr in FY26—and ₹1,778 Cr on a trailing-twelve-month basis through September 2026—while operating margins never fell below 13% even during COVID or the 2024 US freight slump [1]. Better still, GNA did not dilute shareholders to fund that growth: reserves swelled from ₹98 Cr to ₹1,031 Cr purely through retained earnings, with the FY24 equity jump reflecting a 1:1 bonus issue [1][25]. Total borrowings sit at a modest ₹203 Cr against ₹1,074 Cr of equity (0.7x H1 Debt/OPBDIT), though Other Liabilities jumped 52% in six months to ₹453 Cr (pushing TOL/TNW from 0.5x to 0.6x) and consolidated results include two pre-revenue, auditor-unreviewed subsidiaries (GNA Axles Inc. in Michigan and GNA Mobility Limited) [1][4][33][35].

When you check the Cash Flow Statement, earnings quality shows real cyclical working-capital drag. Over FY18–FY26, cumulative Cash Flow from Operations totaled ₹834 Cr against ₹784 Cr of Net Profit—confirming profits are real over a full cycle—while cumulative Free Cash Flow totaled ₹54 Cr across the FCF row, with FY26 alone supplying +₹56 Cr after -₹2 Cr cumulative across FY18–FY25 [1]. Yet FY26 CFO (₹214 Cr) and FCF (+₹56 Cr) were flattered by Days Payable stretching +53 days (76d to 129d), and in H1 FY27 CFO reverted to ₹61.15 Cr against ₹82.34 Cr of PAT (74.3% conversion) while forging presses, SUV cells, and captive solar demand ₹100–125 Cr of annual reinvestment [1][4][33][35]. If supplier credit unwinds from 129 Days Payable and ₹453 Cr Other Liabilities back toward FY22–FY25 norms (76–89 days) during a cyclical pause, working-capital outflows could pull annual CFO negative as in FY17 (-₹90 Cr) [1][35].

Finally, look at the Ratios and H1 FY27 receivables footnotes to understand GNA's structural ceiling. Across ten years, ROCE has hovered between 14% and 21%, finishing FY26 at 14.3% with ROE at 12.2% [1]. The culprit is right there in plain sight: 151 FY26 Debtor Days, ₹698.27 Cr of Trade Receivables as of September 30, 2026 (+19.9% in six months, ~143 days on TTM sales), and ₹312.64 Cr of inventories (+42.7% YoY) [1][4][35]. Meanwhile, while the 2024 family settlement explains Maninder Singh Seehra's full exit on September 29, 2026, promoters retain a 5.49% share pledge (13.80 lakh shares) [12][37]. Until GNA compresses its five-month export collection cycle without payable stretching and proves durable margins through North American Class 8 and U.S. tariff volatility, it remains a well-run, creditworthy cyclical manufacturer—not a high-ROCE capital-light compounder.

book_subsections.title: Why ₹698 Cr of Receivables & 151 Debtor Days Cap ROCE in the 14%–21% Corridor
paragraphs: Look closely at the ten-year capital efficiency math: GNA Axles earned 15%–21% ROCE during the FY18–FY19 and FY23 booms, and 14%–15% during the FY20–FY21 and FY24–FY26 slowdowns (14.3% ROCE and 12.2% ROE in FY26) [1]. Why doesn't a company with 15%–16% operating margins and ₹203 Cr of low-cost debt compound at 25%+ ROCE? Because 151 FY26 Debtor Days and 117 Inventory Days—followed by Trade Receivables climbing to ₹698.27 Cr and inventories to ₹312.64 Cr in H1 FY27—tie up ₹1,213 Cr of Other Assets alongside ₹516 Cr of Fixed Assets and CWIP (NWC/OI ~40% per ICRA) [1][4][33][35]. Until GNA compresses its export collection cycle or shifts decisively into higher-margin machined SUV/EV shafts, its intrinsic business quality is squarely CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL—creditworthy, resilient, and cash-generative over a full cycle, but capital-intensive.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Locking the Business-Quality Baseline Under Fresh Cyclical & Policy Tests
book_callouts.text: Our fundamental audit of GNA Axles yields a clear, unvarnished baseline: GNA is an [ICRA]AA- (Stable) Tier-1 specialist (reaffirmed Nov 13, 2026 at 0.7x H1 Debt/OPBDIT) with real OEM qualification moats, a sharp H1 FY27 revenue rebound (+37% Q1, +50% Q2), low debt, and >₹240 Cr SUV/LV momentum [1][3][4][33]. At the same time, its 14.3% ROCE, 12.2% ROE, ₹698.3 Cr H1 Trade Receivables (74.3% H1 CFO/PAT), ₹453 Cr Other Liabilities payable-unwind risk, 80% top-10 customer concentration, October 2026 North American Class 8 order plunge (-44% YoY), November 25 USTR Section 301 proposed 25% India tariffs atop Section 232 duties, and 5.49% promoter share pledge place it squarely in CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL territory [1][4][12][30][31][33][34][35][37].
